title: "Credit default swaps"

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

## QuantLib set-up

```{r}
#| label: quantlib-setup
act365 <- QuantLib::Actual365Fixed()
act360 <- QuantLib::Actual360()
weekends <- QuantLib::WeekendsOnly()
ql_yield <- function(date, rate) {
  QuantLib::YieldTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::FlatForward(ql_date(date), rate, act365, "Continuous"))
}
ql_hazard <- function(date, hazard) {
  QuantLib::DefaultProbabilityTermStructureHandle(QuantLib::FlatHazardRate(ql_date(date), QuantLib::QuoteHandle(QuantLib::SimpleQuote(hazard)), act365))
}
ql_cds <- function(notional, spread, start, end, rule) {
  schedule <- QuantLib::Schedule(ql_date(start), ql_date(end), QuantLib::Period(3L, "Months"), weekends, "Following", "Unadjusted", rule, FALSE)
  QuantLib::CreditDefaultSwap(QuantLib::Protection_Buyer_get(), notional, spread, schedule, "Following", act360)
}
```

RiemannFinMath has no flat yield curve in its public API. `flat_curve` finds the OIS quotes of a log-linear curve with the requested zero rate; its definition is in @sec-helpers. The rates of the two sides therefore differ by the accuracy of that search.

## One-year swap, MidPoint engine

```{r}
#| label: flat-inputs
flat <- list(trade = "2022-09-19", start = "2022-09-20", maturity = "2023-09-20", notional = 1e7, rate = 0.10, market_spread = 0.013, coupon = 0.01, recovery = 0.4)
flat$hazard <- flat$market_spread / (1 - flat$recovery)
show_inputs(c(flat, list(schedule = "3M, weekends only, following, unadjusted at the end, forward", premium_day_count = "Actual/360")))
```

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: flat-quantlib
ql_set_evaluation_date(flat$trade)
ql_flat <- ql_cds(flat$notional, flat$coupon, flat$start, flat$maturity, "Forward")
QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_flat, QuantLib::MidPointCdsEngine(ql_hazard(flat$trade, flat$hazard), flat$recovery, ql_yield(flat$trade, flat$rate)))
ql_flat_curve <- QuantLib::FlatHazardRate(ql_date(flat$trade), QuantLib::QuoteHandle(QuantLib::SimpleQuote(flat$hazard)), act365)
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: flat-riemann
flat_rates <- flat_curve(flat$trade, flat$rate)
flat_hazard <- RiemannFinMath::hazard_curve(flat$trade, "2060-01-01", flat$hazard)
flat_swap <- RiemannFinMath::credit_default_swap("buyer", flat$notional, flat$coupon, flat$start, flat$maturity)
riemann_flat <- RiemannFinMath::cds_value(flat_swap, flat_hazard, flat$recovery, flat_rates, flat$trade, "midpoint")
print(flat_swap)
print(flat_hazard)
```

```{r}
#| label: flat-results
bind_rows(
  compare_values("Yield curve: discount at maturity", "discount factor", exp(-flat$rate * as.numeric(as.Date(flat$maturity) - as.Date(flat$trade)) / 365), RiemannFinMath::discount(flat_rates, flat$maturity), "Formula of the flat curve"),
  compare_values("Survival at maturity", "probability", ql_flat_curve$survivalProbability(ql_date(flat$maturity)), RiemannFinMath::survival_probability(flat_hazard, flat$maturity)),
  compare_values("NPV", "currency", ql_flat$NPV(), riemann_flat$npv),
  compare_values("Coupon leg", "currency", ql_flat$couponLegNPV(), riemann_flat$coupon_leg_npv),
  compare_values("Default leg", "currency", ql_flat$defaultLegNPV(), riemann_flat$default_leg_npv),
  compare_values("Fair spread", "bp", 1e4 * ql_flat$fairSpread(), 1e4 * riemann_flat$fair_spread)
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Hazard rate at zero NPV

Both sides use the solver of the legacy text, R's `uniroot`, around their own valuation of a swap whose coupon is the market spread.

```{r}
#| label: flat-hazard
ql_market <- ql_cds(flat$notional, flat$market_spread, flat$start, flat$maturity, "Forward")
ql_at_hazard <- function(h) {
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_market, QuantLib::MidPointCdsEngine(ql_hazard(flat$trade, h), flat$recovery, ql_yield(flat$trade, flat$rate)))
  ql_market$NPV()
}
market_swap <- RiemannFinMath::credit_default_swap("buyer", flat$notional, flat$market_spread, flat$start, flat$maturity)
riemann_at_hazard <- function(h) {
  RiemannFinMath::cds_value(market_swap, RiemannFinMath::hazard_curve(flat$trade, "2060-01-01", h), flat$recovery, flat_rates, flat$trade, "midpoint")$npv
}
compare_values(
  "Hazard rate", "percent",
  100 * uniroot(ql_at_hazard, c(1e-8, 0.5), tol = 1e-10)$root,
  100 * uniroot(riemann_at_hazard, c(1e-8, 0.5), tol = 1e-10)$root
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Standard five-year swap, ISDA and MidPoint engines

```{r}
#| label: isda-inputs
isda <- list(trade = "2022-08-19", notional = 1e7, market_spread = 30.426 / 1e4, coupon = 0.01, recovery = 0.4, rate = 0.0025)
show_inputs(c(isda, list(tenor = "5Y", rule = "CDS2015", premium_day_count = "Actual/360")))
```

```{r}
#| label: isda-maturity
ql_set_evaluation_date(isda$trade)
isda$maturity <- ql_iso(QuantLib::cdsMaturity(ql_date(isda$trade), QuantLib::Period(5L, "Years"), "CDS2015"))
riemann_maturity <- RiemannFinMath::cds_maturity(isda$trade, "5Y", "cds2015")
compare_values("Maturity of a standard swap", "days", as.numeric(isda$maturity), as.numeric(riemann_maturity)) |>
  show_results()
```

The hazard rate is solved once on the QuantLib side, as in the legacy text, and given to both.

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: isda-quantlib
ql_market_isda <- ql_cds(isda$notional, isda$market_spread, isda$trade, isda$maturity, "CDS2015")
ql_isda_at_hazard <- function(h) {
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_market_isda, QuantLib::IsdaCdsEngine(ql_hazard(isda$trade, h), isda$recovery, ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate)))
  ql_market_isda$NPV()
}
isda$hazard <- uniroot(ql_isda_at_hazard, c(1e-8, 0.5), tol = 1e-10)$root
ql_standard <- ql_cds(isda$notional, isda$coupon, isda$trade, isda$maturity, "CDS2015")
ql_engines <- list(
  isda = QuantLib::IsdaCdsEngine(ql_hazard(isda$trade, isda$hazard), isda$recovery, ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate)),
  midpoint = QuantLib::MidPointCdsEngine(ql_hazard(isda$trade, isda$hazard), isda$recovery, ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate))
)
ql_values <- imap(ql_engines, \(engine, name) {
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_standard, engine)
  tibble(
    engine = name, npv = ql_standard$NPV(), coupon = ql_standard$couponLegNPV(), default = ql_standard$defaultLegNPV(),
    rebate = tryCatch(ql_standard$accrualRebateNPV(), error = \(e) NA_real_), fair_spread = ql_standard$fairSpread(),
    fair_upfront = tryCatch(ql_standard$fairUpfront(), error = \(e) NA_real_)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: isda-riemann
isda_rates <- flat_curve(isda$trade, isda$rate)
isda_hazard <- RiemannFinMath::hazard_curve(isda$trade, "2060-01-01", isda$hazard)
standard_swap <- RiemannFinMath::credit_default_swap("buyer", isda$notional, isda$coupon, isda$trade, isda$maturity, rule = "cds2015")
riemann_values <- map(c("isda", "midpoint"), \(engine) {
  RiemannFinMath::cds_value(standard_swap, isda_hazard, isda$recovery, isda_rates, isda$trade, engine) |>
    mutate(engine = engine)
}) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: isda-results
compare_or_absent <- function(item, unit, quantlib, riemann) {
  if (is.na(quantlib)) {
    not_comparable(item, unit, NA_real_, riemann, "QuantLib returns no value for a swap made with this constructor")
  } else {
    compare_values(item, unit, quantlib, riemann)
  }
}
map(c("isda", "midpoint"), \(name) {
  q <- ql_values |> filter(engine == name)
  r <- riemann_values |> filter(engine == name)
  bind_rows(
    compare_values(paste(name, "NPV"), "currency", q$npv, r$npv),
    compare_values(paste(name, "coupon leg"), "currency", q$coupon, r$coupon_leg_npv),
    compare_values(paste(name, "default leg"), "currency", q$default, r$default_leg_npv),
    compare_or_absent(paste(name, "accrual rebate"), "currency", q$rebate, r$accrual_rebate_npv),
    compare_values(paste(name, "fair spread"), "bp", 1e4 * q$fair_spread, 1e4 * r$fair_spread),
    compare_or_absent(paste(name, "fair upfront"), "percent of notional", 100 * q$fair_upfront, 100 * r$fair_upfront)
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_results()
```

## The legacy text's swap builder

The legacy text makes this swap with QuantLib's `MakeCreditDefaultSwap`, through GaussQuant, which sets a trade date and cash settlement days. `credit_default_swap` has neither argument, so the swap above uses the plain constructor on both sides. These rows show what that leaves out. They are not judged, because the swaps are not the same.

```{r}
#| label: isda-builder
legacy_swap <- function(spread, engine) {
  GaussQuant::make_cds_GQL(
    maturity_date = isda$maturity, running_spread = spread, notional = isda$notional, side = "buyer", trade_date = isda$trade,
    coupon_tenor = "3M", day_counter = "Actual360", date_generation_rule = "CDS2015", pricing_engine = engine
  )
}
legacy_engine <- function(h) QuantLib::IsdaCdsEngine(ql_hazard(isda$trade, h), isda$recovery, ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate))
legacy_hazard <- uniroot(\(h) legacy_swap(isda$market_spread, legacy_engine(h))$NPV(), c(1e-8, 0.5), tol = 1e-10)$root
legacy_value <- legacy_swap(isda$coupon, legacy_engine(legacy_hazard))
riemann_on_legacy <- RiemannFinMath::cds_value(
  standard_swap, RiemannFinMath::hazard_curve(isda$trade, "2060-01-01", legacy_hazard), isda$recovery, isda_rates, isda$trade, "isda"
)
reason <- "The builder sets a trade date and cash settlement days; RiemannFinMath's swap has neither"
bind_rows(
  not_comparable("NPV", "currency", legacy_value$NPV(), riemann_on_legacy$npv, reason, "QuantLib builder via GaussQuant"),
  not_comparable("Accrual rebate", "currency", legacy_value$accrualRebateNPV(), riemann_on_legacy$accrual_rebate_npv, reason, "QuantLib builder via GaussQuant"),
  not_comparable("Fair upfront", "percent of notional", 100 * legacy_value$fairUpfront(), 100 * riemann_on_legacy$fair_upfront, reason, "QuantLib builder via GaussQuant")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Bootstrap from a spread term structure

The legacy text solves one flat hazard rate. This item has no example there, and the spreads are synthetic, ending near the market spread above.

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-inputs
term <- tibble(years = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 7L, 10L), spread = c(0.0012, 0.0018, 0.0024, 0.0030, 0.0034, 0.0037))
knitr::kable(term |> mutate(spread_bp = 1e4 * spread, .keep = "unused"), digits = 4, caption = "Running spreads")
show_inputs(list(evaluation = isda$trade, recovery = isda$recovery, rate = isda$rate, schedule = "3M, weekends only, following, backward, settlement 0 days"))
```

QuantLib:

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-quantlib
ql_bootstrap <- function(spreads, engine_model) {
  helpers <- QuantLib::DefaultProbabilityHelperVector()
  walk2(term$years, spreads, \(y, s) {
    helpers$append(QuantLib::SpreadCdsHelper(
      s, QuantLib::Period(y, "Years"), 0L, weekends, "Quarterly", "Following", "Backward", act360, isda$recovery,
      ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate), TRUE, TRUE, QuantLib::Date(), act360, TRUE, engine_model
    ))
  })
  QuantLib::PiecewiseFlatHazardRate(ql_date(isda$trade), helpers, act365)
}
ql_set_evaluation_date(isda$trade)
models <- list(midpoint = QuantLib::CreditDefaultSwap_Midpoint_get(), isda = QuantLib::CreditDefaultSwap_ISDA_get())
ql_curves <- map(models, \(m) ql_bootstrap(term$spread, m))
node_dates <- map(ql_curves, \(curve) ql_date_vector(curve$dates())[-1] |> map(ql_iso) |> list_c())
# QuantLib's nodes are adjusted dates. The swaps end on the unadjusted date, which goes to RiemannFinMath.
unadjusted_maturities <- as.Date(isda$trade) %m+% years(term$years)
ql_survival <- map(ql_curves, \(curve) {
  map_dbl(ql_date_vector(curve$dates())[-1], \(d) curve$survivalProbability(d))
})
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-riemann
riemann_curves <- imap(models, \(m, engine) {
  RiemannFinMath::bootstrap_hazard_curve(isda$trade, unadjusted_maturities, term$spread, isda$recovery, isda_rates, engine)
})
```

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap-results
imap(ql_survival, \(q, engine) {
  compare_values(
    paste(engine, term$years, "years"), "survival probability", q,
    RiemannFinMath::survival_probability(riemann_curves[[engine]], node_dates[[engine]])
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_results()
```

## Sensitivity to the spreads and the recovery

QuantLib rebuilds the hazard curve with a bump of 1e-6. RiemannFinMath uses automatic differentiation and the implicit function theorem.

```{r}
#| label: sensitivity
risk_inputs <- list(notional = 1e7, coupon = 0.01, start = "2022-08-20", end = "2027-09-20")
show_inputs(risk_inputs)
ql_risk_swap <- ql_cds(risk_inputs$notional, risk_inputs$coupon, risk_inputs$start, risk_inputs$end, "Forward")
ql_value_on <- function(spreads, recovery = isda$recovery) {
  curve <- QuantLib::DefaultProbabilityTermStructureHandle(ql_bootstrap(spreads, models$midpoint))
  QuantLib::Instrument_setPricingEngine(ql_risk_swap, QuantLib::MidPointCdsEngine(curve, recovery, ql_yield(isda$trade, isda$rate)))
  ql_risk_swap$NPV()
}
h <- 1e-6
ql_spread_risk <- map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(term)), \(i) {
  move <- function(sign) {
    spreads <- term$spread
    spreads[i] <- spreads[i] + sign * h
    ql_value_on(spreads)
  }
  (move(1) - move(-1)) / (2 * h) * 1e-4
})
ql_recovery_risk <- (ql_value_on(term$spread, isda$recovery + 1e-4) - ql_value_on(term$spread, isda$recovery - 1e-4)) / 2e-4 * 0.01

riemann_risk_swap <- RiemannFinMath::credit_default_swap("buyer", risk_inputs$notional, risk_inputs$coupon, risk_inputs$start, risk_inputs$end)
riemann_risk <- RiemannFinMath::cds_quote_sensitivity(riemann_risk_swap, riemann_curves$midpoint, isda_rates, isda$trade, "midpoint")
bind_rows(
  compare_values(paste("Spread", term$years, "years"), "currency per bp", ql_spread_risk, riemann_risk$npv_per_bp),
  compare_values("Recovery, hazard curve fixed", "currency per percent", ql_recovery_risk, riemann_risk$npv_per_recovery_percent[1])
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,          ~QuantLib,                                               ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Swap",           "`Schedule`, then `CreditDefaultSwap` with a side object", "One call with names; conventions have example defaults",
  "Wrapper", "Curves",         "Handles of term structures",                            "Values; a hazard curve from dates and rates",
  "Wrapper", "Flat yield curve", "`FlatForward`",                                       "No constructor; quotes must be fitted",
  "Wrapper", "Engine",         "An object set on the swap",                             "A name in the valuation call",
  "Core",    "Legs",           "Stored in the instrument after a lazy calculation",     "A value returned by a pure function",
  "Core",    "Bootstrap",      "Helpers in a piecewise template",                       "A function; the nodes are returned as a table",
  "Core",    "Risk",           "Not exposed; finite differences by the caller",         "Automatic differentiation and the implicit function theorem"
) |>
  show_design()
```
